messages:
zoe: Hey everyone, first week here. Running the local stack with docker-compose and migrations fail with `ERROR: extension \"vector\" does not exist` during a migration that creates an index using pgvector. I'm using `image: postgres:14` in compose. Anyone run into this locally?

amir: Welcome! Pgvector is a C extension that isn't bundled in the vanilla Postgres image by default. You have a few options: use a prebuilt image that includes pgvector, install/build the extension in a custom image, or create the extension in the DB if it's already available.

pat: Quick repro checks: 1) Is the DB volume fresh? `docker-compose up` only runs init scripts on an empty DB. 2) Can you exec into the container and run `psql -U postgres -c "\dx"` to list extensions? That will show whether `vector` is installed.

zoe: I ran `docker-compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -c "\dx"` and it shows no vector. The volume is fresh (I `docker-compose down -v` before).

julia: Easiest dev route: use a postgres image that already packages the extension. Example Docker Hub images like `ankane/pgvector` exist (they bundle pgvector for certain PG majors). So in compose:```
services:
  postgres:
    image: ankane/pgvector:14
    volumes:
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
```
This image includes the extension so your migration's `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;` will succeed on init.

amir: If you prefer to stick to upstream postgres, you can build a small Dockerfile that installs the extension during image build (requires build deps):```
FROM postgres:14
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential git postgresql-server-dev-14 && \
    git clone https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector.git /tmp/pgvector && \
    cd /tmp/pgvector && make && make install && rm -rf /tmp/pgvector && apt-get remove -y build-essential git postgresql-server-dev-14 && apt-get autoremove -y && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```
Then use your custom image in compose. Note: longer build time, but works reliably.

pat: Also remember the init order: `docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` scripts only run when the container initializes a brand new database cluster. If you already have a persisted volume, create the extension manually:```
docker-compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -c "CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;"
```or run `psql` from a client container.

zoe: Great info. For local dev I don't care about clean builds, so I switched to `ankane/pgvector:14` and added a `./db/init/00-create-vector.sql` with `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;`. Migrations now run fine.

julia: Another tip: pin the pg image in compose and add a short note in README about the pgvector requirement so other new hires don't hit the same wall. Also add healthcheck so migrations wait for DB readiness.

amir: If anyone runs into build problems on M1/ARM, some prebuilt images might be amd64-only; you can force platform or build locally for arm64. We added a short paragraph in dev docs about pgvector images and ARM issues.

infra-bot: Dev docs updated with a pgvector local dev recipe and example compose snippets: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/dev-setup#pgvector (cc @new-hires) :book:
